currentSummary:
Projected Final Standings (10-Team League)

Quick honest caveat: this is inherently a roster-talent guess, not a hard prediction — health, waiver activity, and matchup luck will decide the real thing. But going purely off what's actually on these rosters:

The field is tougher than just "our 4 vs. the rest" — a couple of the other teams are legitimately stacked. **RickBinkerson** landed Jonathan Taylor plus a Lamar Jackson keeper (arguably the single best keeper value in the whole league) on top of a London/Higgins/Waddle receiver room. **JONTHETANK** somehow has both De'Von Achane and Saquon Barkley plus Joe Burrow — an absurd RB1/RB2 combo. Those two rosters are real threats to finish above all four of you.

Among the four of you, here's how I'd stack it up based on the draft:

**Caleb — 11-3, 1st**
The keeper bonanza (JSN + Warren on top of Chase/Henry/Hurts) gives this roster the highest floor and ceiling of the four. I'd favor this team over the outside competition too.

**Ben — 9-5, 3rd**
Cleanest, lowest-variance build of the bunch, but Rick's and JONTHETANK's rosters are strong enough that I can't put Ben ahead of both.

**Kyle — 8-6, 4th**
Excellent balanced team (McBride discount, Nabers, Wilson), just fewer top-5-overall-caliber assets than Caleb or Ben.

**Mason — 7-7, 5th** 
Real upside if Rice returns to 2023 form, but that ACL recovery (plus banking on Dobbins/Kittle staying healthy) is genuine variance the other three teams don't carry as much of.

If Rice comes back fully healthy early, bump Mason up a couple spots — that's the single biggest swing factor on any of these four rosters.

weeklyRoasts.roast: A :Jahmyr Gibbs at 1.1 is about as close to a free roll as this format allows — he's the consensus #1 overall player in PPR right now. But the real standout is the Chase Brown keeper — Brown's broken out hard enough that he's currently going in the RB8-10 range overall (roughly a late-1st/early-2nd), and you're getting him as a Round 2 keeper. That's not a value, that's a heist. Sam LaPorta falling to you in Round 6 is another quiet win — legit TE1-tier production a full 4-5 rounds after where TEs of his caliber usually go. From there it's clean, sensible depth all the way down (Egbuka, Adams, Hubbard) with zero real reaches. If there's a nitpick, it's that the roster plays it a little safe late — no real boom-or-bust dart throws, just solid vets and a couple of rookie fliers (Dart, Lemon). Efficient, low-drama, no regrets.

A+ :This is the best-constructed roster of the four, and it's not close. Ja'Marr Chase at 1.3 is a top-5-overall lock. Then Jaxon Smith-Njigba as a Round 2 keeper — JSN is now a consensus top-5 overall PPR asset himself, meaning you're getting a literal 1st-round talent two full rounds after where he actually belongs. Derrick Henry sliding to you at pick 23 is a gift most leagues wouldn't allow. Jalen Hurts at pick 58 is the kind of positional-value play that wins leagues — a rushing-floor QB1 for the price of a flex. And then Tyler Warren as a Round 9 keeper on top of all that, for a tight end who broke out hard enough to be TE1-caliber territory now. I genuinely can't find a bad pick on this board — even the depth (Pollard, Metcalf, Corum) is sensible. The only thing keeping this from being a perfect draft is that with this much value banked early, the pressure's now entirely on you not to overthink the waiver wire into oblivion.

A- :Smart, balanced build. McCaffrey at 1.6 is fair value with real bust risk baked in (injury history is injury history), but Trey McBride — this year's consensus TE1 — falling to Round 2 is a legitimate coup; getting the best tight end in the format a full round after where he "should" go is the kind of thing that changes a season. Malik Nabers and Garrett Wilson both landing on the same roster gives you two true alpha WR1 talents, which is a genuinely enviable receiver room for a 10-team league. The double-dip on rushing QBs (Jayden Daniels, then Mahomes as a luxury QB2 in Round 11) is a nice hedge, though Daniels does carry real injury-availability questions worth watching. The Chris Olave keeper at Round 6 is fine value, not a robbery — the honest one of the bunch. Cam Skattebo as a Round 9 keeper is a solid, low-cost swing on a rookie who flashed. Nothing to actually criticize here, just slightly less absurd value than Caleb's board.

A- : Justin Jefferson at 1.8 is a proven stud landing at fair value in a year where he's oddly gone as low as WR5 in some rankings — good, not flashy. The real headline is the Kenneth Walker keeper at Round 3 — his current ADP has him firmly in the RB9-ish range (basically a 2nd-round player now), so locking him in three rounds later than that is excellent value. The Rashee Rice keeper at Round 5, though, is the one genuine boom-or-bust swing on this board — he's still working back from a torn ACL, so this is a bet on 2023-form Rice returning, not a locked-in asset like Walker. That's not a criticism so much as an honest flag: this roster has more variance riding on health than the other three. The rest of the build is sound — Omarion Hampton as a real bell-cow rookie flier in Round 2, George Kittle as steady TE depth, and a sensible trio of developing QB darts late (Caleb Williams, Bo Nix) giving you optionality if the Jefferson/Hampton floor holds. Slightly spicier than Ben's or Kyle's boards, but the ceiling's real if Rice comes back right.
